disagreements.topic: Pipeline route across state trust land: denied twice, and is it fatal?
disagreements.positions: agent_4 says the NM State Land Office denied the Green Chile pipeline's state-trust-land right-of-way twice with 'no disclosed reroute', so a Jupiter slip past 2028 is plausible and it keeps a 25% bear weight; agents 1, 2, 3, 5 treat the pipeline only as a slip of the in-service date to ~Feb 1, 2027.
disagreements.resolution: The 'denied twice' claim is correct: Commissioner Garcia Richard cancelled the right-of-way applications and a meter-station lease on March 20, 2026 and denied Energy Transfer's reconsideration request on July 14, 2026. But the denied segment is only ~0.63 miles of a ~17.8-mile lateral, and the project did not stall: BLM authorized the federal-land crossing (16 miles) on May 6, 2026; the lateral is under a FERC environmental assessment in docket CP26-80-000 (EA issued Sep 4, comments due Oct 5, 90-day federal authorization decision deadline Dec 3, 2026), with the company rerouting the state-land segment. 'No disclosed reroute' is therefore wrong. The pipeline is a real timing risk: Feb 1, 2027 leaves about two months after a Dec 3 decision, and rehearing or litigation is likely. It is not a route-level dead end.
disagreements.evidence: NM State Land Office letter of Jul 14, 2026; Pipeline & Gas Journal (Jul 2026); Source NM (Mar 31, 2026); BLM release (May 6, 2026); Federal Register EA notices (Jul 29 and Sep 10, 2026; govinfo copies, src 5-6).

disagreements.topic: Status of the fuel-cell air-quality permit (Nov 23, 2026 deadline)
disagreements.positions: agent_3 says the permit hearing was held Sep 14; agent_5 says no hearing officer has been appointed; agents 1, 2, 4 treat Nov 23 as a decision binary.
disagreements.resolution: No hearing has been held. The Sep 14 hearing was halted: hearing officer Max Shepherd recused himself (order dated Aug 22, reported Aug 24) while an NM Supreme Court stay paused the proceeding; the court lifted the stays on Sep 17. NMED named retired federal judge James Browning as the new hearing officer on Oct 2 (Albuquerque Journal), but no opening date has been announced, and the state Attorney General backs the challengers. State law lets NMED extend its deadline for good cause, so the likeliest outcome is an extension and a drawn-out overhang, not an approve/deny binary on Nov 23. agent_3 is wrong on the hearing and agent_5 is right.
disagreements.evidence: Albuquerque Journal (Aug 24, Sep 17 and Oct 2, 2026; src 8, 9, 26); Organ Mountain News on the AG's position; Searchlight NM / Source NM on the extension-for-good-cause provision.

disagreements.topic: How much Jupiter matters to the 12-month price
disagreements.positions: Bear weights range from 23% (agent_5) to 30% (agent_1); all now call Jupiter mostly a timing risk. agent_4 alone argues a slip past 2028 is plausible.
disagreements.resolution: Both Jupiter gates (the FERC pipeline decision due Dec 3 and the NMED air permit, likely extended) now sit late in 2026 or later, with organized opposition at the state level. That raises the odds that some Jupiter shipments slip from 2027 into 2028 and that the Feb 2027 FY27 guide is conservative on Oracle. Offsetting factors: Jupiter is outside 2026 guidance and the units can be redeployed. This justifies a small downward nudge in the middle of the ladder, not a larger bear case.

disagreements.positions: Base round: the agents' research targets were $222-245 (mean $234.6), all below the $288.70 close of 2026-09-25 (src 27); P/E legs $260-280 on 38-55x; DCF legs $122-165.
disagreements.resolution: No factual error remains after round 1; the spread comes from differences in multiples and DCF assumptions. Every blend is below spot, while ladder medians sit at ~$265-282. That gap reflects momentum and a fat right tail, which the ladders already carry. This build (2026-10-23) replaces those blends: research target (12m) $185.84 vs the $193.30 close of 2026-10-23.

confidence_reason: The searches settled the facts: the pipeline was denied twice but rerouted and is under FERC review with a Dec 3 decision, and the air-permit hearing has not happened. These facts argue only for a small shift of Jupiter revenue from 2027 into 2028, which most agents had already priced qualitatively. The change is therefore a nudge of about 0.5pt, not a settled disagreement that clearly matters.
thesis_break_reason: Reviewed 2026-10-23 after the Oct 22 Q3 print (kept at $150): at ~$150 BE would trade at ~29x the build's horizon NTM GAAP EPS (~$5.12) with FY2026 revenue already raised to $4.4-4.6B, which only makes sense with real cuts to product_gw or product_gm. $150 is 22% below the $193.30 close of 2026-10-23 and below the $163.75 post-Q2 close of 2026-07-29 (src 27), and ~28x the post-print FY2027 consensus EPS of $5.31 (src 25), with net debt near zero ($16.2M, converts carried as debt). That only makes sense with real estimate cuts: FERC denying or courts blocking the rerouted Green Chile lateral, or the air permit being denied rather than extended, with no redeployment of the 2.4 GW; a Feb 2027 FY27 guide well below ~$7B revenue; gross margin under ~30%; a scandium supply disruption; or an AI-capex pullback. A permit-deadline extension or a pipeline slip of a few months is not a thesis break.

summary: In the base round (2026-09-25) the five revised forecasts clustered tightly: research targets $222-245 (mean ~$235) and P(>= spot) 0.46-0.49. The one contested fact checks out but is less damaging than it sounds. New Mexico did deny the Jupiter pipeline's state-land crossing twice (Mar 20 and Jul 14), but the denial covers ~0.63 miles, and the rerouted lateral is under FERC review with a Dec 3 decision. Separately, the air-permit hearing has not yet been held, so the Nov 23 deadline will probably be extended. I nudge the middle of the ladder down ~0.5pt for a likelier slip of Jupiter revenue into 2028; confidence is low, and the forecast stays near the mean with a median just below spot. The driver-led build of 2026-10-23 sets the research target (12m) at $185.84, below the $193.30 close.

reconciled_inputs.structure_note: Driver-led backlog-and-capacity build (ai_industrials primary method) valued with horizon multiples on the build's own NTM figures at 2027-10-23 (~19% FY2027 + 81% FY2028). Five drivers (product_gw, product_asp, product_gm, opex, factory_gw) compute Product revenue, Product EBIT and capacity capex; installation/service/electricity is a plain segment (~12% of FY2026 revenue). Legs: P/E 40x NTM GAAP (0.6), EV/EBITDA 26x (0.2) and EV/sales 5.5x (0.2) as peer cross-checks. No DCF leg (not a neocloud). No signed-contract piece: no Bloom contract discloses term, price and counterparty together (Oracle 2.4 GW, AEP 1 GW frameworks undisclosed in price). Converts: the $2.5B 0% notes due Nov 2030 convert at $194.97 (12.82M shares, 10-K src 16). The set's value sits below that price, so they are carried as debt at principal: net debt (estimate) = $2,500.0M 2030 notes + $2.95M Korean JV loan - $2,486.7M cash = $16.2M (10-Q debt table src 15, F75); the $22.8M 2029 Green Notes (conversion $20.84, in the money) count as equity. Diluted shares (estimate) = 295.66M outstanding at Oct 19 (F81) + 15.61M options/awards (Q3) + 1.09M 2029-note shares = 312.4M, without the 2030 notes' 12.82M. The base agents treated the converts as equity (net cash ~$2.45B on ~324M shares); here that changes the result by -2.3% (below the 5% line; kept as a note). Legs not driver-linked: none (all legs read the driven rows).
reconciled_inputs.gap_note: Tax 5/10/15% is an estimate (NOLs; 2026 YTD tax $2.7M on $524M pretax, F66/F73). Peer forward multiples could not be built: Bigdata.com credits were exhausted, Alpha Vantage hit its daily limit and Twelve Data estimates need a higher plan, so the peer legs rest on trailing (TTM) multiples from filings. Post-print consensus comes from the stockanalysis.com forecast page (2026-10-23, src 25): FY2026 revenue $4.53B and EPS $3.26, FY2027 revenue $7.05B and EPS $5.31.
reconciled_inputs.reverse_dcf_check: 40x NTM GAAP earnings at the horizon implies ~20%+ earnings growth for about five years after FY2028 with margins near 23% EBIT, i.e. capacity growing toward the 5 GW Fremont ceiling.

model.reasoning: Primary method (ai_industrials playbook): backlog-and-capacity driver build over FY2026-28, valued with horizon multiples on the build's own NTM figures at 2027-10-23 (19% FY2027 + 81% FY2028). Five drivers compute the line items: product revenue = product_gw x product_asp (1.24 / 1.80 / 2.50 GW at $3,195 / 3,250 / 3,250 per kW), Product EBIT = revenue x product_gm (37.0 / 37.5 / 37.0%) - opex ($723M / 900M / 1,060M), capex = 4.5% of revenue + $125M per GW of new capacity (factory_gw 2 GW end-2026, 3 GW during 2027). Revenue $4.52B / $6.55B / $8.96B; GAAP EBIT $780M / $1,350M / $2,022M. Cross-checks: P/E 40x NTM GAAP (0.6; peer GAAP P/E TTM median 39.9x), EV/EBITDA 26x (0.2; peer TTM median 24.1x), EV/sales 5.5x (0.2; peer TTM median 5.2x). No DCF leg, no signed-contract piece (no contract discloses term, price and counterparty). Guided metrics (FY2026, guide of 2026-10-22): revenue $4.4-4.6B, record-adjusted $4.61B (median +2.4% vs first-guide midpoints FY2022-25), post-print consensus $4.53B, ours $4.52B, inside; non-GAAP GM ~34%, record-adjusted 34.6%, ours ~34.0%, inside; non-GAAP operating income $960-1,030M, record-adjusted $1,345M (record +23%/+47% but Q4 is pinned by YTD), ours ~$1,015M, inside; non-GAAP EPS $3.10-3.40 (no EPS record; op-income proxy), ours ~$3.19, inside. FY2027 has no guide: ours $6.55B vs post-print consensus $7.05B (-7.1%, stockanalysis.com 2026-10-23). What this build changed vs the base round's 234.60 (mean of five agent values on P/E, EV/sales and DCF legs, no gate record): P/E is applied to GAAP earnings (after ~$230-300M of stock comp) to match the peers' GAAP basis, where the agents put ~40x on non-GAAP; EV/sales 5.5x replaces the agents' 7.5-10x; the DCF legs (20-25% weight at $122-165) are dropped; converts are carried as debt because the value sits below their $194.97 conversion price (net debt $16.2M, 312.4M diluted shares, both estimates with the arithmetic in inputs_detail). The $/kW path is a flagged judgment; at the 36Kr-implied ~$3,040/kW the value is $168.99 (-9.1%). The Q3 print (revenue $1,235.8M, product GM 37.9%, third raise of the FY2026 guide) supports the FY2026 path; the value hinges on capacity beyond 2 GW (judgment call 1). Peers: 4 whole-company + 2 segment-only, trailing only (flag).
